mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) reduce the cost of capital for corporations, increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate sustained accommodative policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in over 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in over 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals dual monetary tightening and economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks dominate market sentiment.
failure_condition: When both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise simultaneously, SPX 5-day returns are positive in over 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in HOUST is followed by positive SPX 20-day returns in over 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in over 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals excessive labor market tightness that may trigger inflation and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in over 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and INDPRO decline, SPX 20-day returns are positive in over 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recoveries, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening economic activity and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-recession recoveries, a rise in INDPRO is followed by negative SPX 60-day returns in over 60% of cases.
